title: Diversity in the Living World — 40-Minute Lesson Plan
subject: Science
objectives: Recognise the variety of plants and animals around us as biodiversity.
Group plants as herbs, shrubs, or trees using stem and height clues.
Group animals by habitat, food, or movement.
Apply simple yes/no questions to classify a plant or animal.
prerequisites: Familiarity with naming common plants and animals.
Basic idea of comparing 'big and small' or 'soft and hard'.
materials: Pictures or printouts of cow, fish, frog, eagle, lion, ant, sparrow
Real or printed leaves: tulsi, mango, grass, hibiscus
A piece of chart paper and coloured markers per group

activities.description: Lay out animal and plant pictures on a desk. Ask: 'How many different living things can we name in 60 seconds?' Make a quick list on the board. Then ask: 'Why is the world full of so many kinds?' Lead into biodiversity.

Group activity: groups of 4 receive 4 leaves and 4 animal pictures. They classify the leaves into 'parallel-veined' vs 'reticulate-veined' and the animals into any TWO groupings of their choice. Each group prepares a chart paper with labels.
teacher_actions: Walk around and prompt with questions
student_actions: Make a chart with two clear groupings

activities.description: Mini-lecture: define biodiversity and the practical reasons we group living things. Introduce herb/shrub/tree by stem height/hardness. Introduce parallel vs reticulate venation, dicot vs monocot. For animals, introduce groupings by habitat (land/water/air/both), food (herb-/carn-/omnivore), and movement.
teacher_actions: Use a mind map on the board
Show 1-2 real-world examples for each category
Connect leaf venation to root system and seed type

activities.description: Each group presents their chart paper. The class judges whether each grouping is consistent (one rule used at a time). The teacher then introduces a 'simple key' approach: a yes/no question chain to identify a plant or animal. Try a sample key live with one of the leaves.
teacher_actions: Ask probing questions about each grouping

activities.description: Quick check: 4 questions — name a herb, a shrub, and a tree; classify the frog by habitat and food; identify whether a parallel-veined leaf likely has tap or fibrous roots; tell why we group living things.
student_actions: Reflect on what they got right

activities.description: Homework: collect (or sketch) any 5 plants near home. Note for each: (i) herb/shrub/tree, (ii) leaf venation, (iii) any flower colour. Bring the table to next class.
teacher_actions: Remind students not to pluck many leaves
student_actions: Promise not to harm the plants

homework: Plant observation table (5 plants) with type, leaf venation, and flower colour.
Read the chapter summary on the Learn page and write 3 'I learned…' lines.
assessment_ideas: Use 5 questions from the bank: 1 MCQ on herbs/shrubs/trees, 1 on venation, 1 on animal habitat, 1 short answer on biodiversity, 1 on adaptations.
Use a small drawing as evidence — students draw two plants and label features.
Use a 'sort the cards' activity in pairs.
references: NCERT Class 6 Science 'Curiosity', Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World
Chapter mind map on the Learn page
